headline: Voters in Mandan, North Dakota, will decide on 15 December whether to ban large-scale data centers in their city.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the election was called on 6 Oct 2026, so the pool item is a late repost, and the proposed ban's details are not given.
importance_line: Residents of a small city will decide directly whether big AI data centers can be built there, which others may copy, but the exact limits of the proposed ban are not yet clear.
summary: The Bismarck Tribune reports that Mandan, North Dakota, will hold a special election on 15 Dec 2026 on whether to ban large-scale data centers, after the city verified a citizen petition; the city commission set the vote at its meeting on 6 Oct. Dakota News Network adds that the vote comes on top of next month's midterm election and that a separate special election to fill the seat of commissioner Craig Sjoberg, who died in August, has no date yet.
